BLOCKER: Diff ships only a cron file; no Go PITR check, drill/reconcile/region-guard logic, or the required tests appear — acceptance criteria and the language rule (new logic → Go) are unmet by what is under review.

/etc/cron.d lines lack the mandatory user field: `17 * * * * pfbackupdrill --command ...` parses `pfbackupdrill` as the user and `--command ...` as the command, so every drill silently fails or is rejected.
File begins with a UTF-8 BOM (`﻿`) before the first comment; cron does not treat BOM-prefixed lines as comments and may refuse the entire file.
MAJOR: Cron lines expand `$PF_BACKUP_DRILL_REPORT_DIR`, `$PF_DRILL_TENANT`, `$PF_DB_DSN` but the file never assigns them (only a comment mentions "Env"); /etc/cron.d does not inherit shell/profile env, so drills run with empty tenant/report dir/DSN.

The `status` staleness check uses `--max-age-hours 26` yet only covers daily drills; the weekly tenant drill (7-day cadence) will always look stale or is unchecked, producing false alerts or blind spots.

Failures are observability-dead: output goes only to `/var/log/backup-drill.log` with no rotation, and "cron mail/alert" assumes a configured MTA that is unlikely to exist — failed drills can go unnoticed indefinitely.

Destructive daily restore (`PF_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DRILL=1`, scratch DB create/drop) runs unattended with no concurrency guard, freeze window, or confirmation the target DSN is staging, risking interference with live traffic.
MINOR: Fixed, guessable scratch DB names (`pf_scratch_daily`, `pf_scratch_tenant`) collide across overlapping runs and leave residue if a drill is killed mid-way.
Log redirection is duplicated per line instead of a single `LOG` variable or wrapper, making rotation/destination changes error-prone.
Hourly PITR check logs to the same file as daily drills, burying actionable PITR failures in a high-volume stream.
NIT: Comment references "EDP-23" while the item is BI-PF-1315; traceability would be clearer with both identifiers.
`# Alert hook:` comment promises behavior (missing/failed/stale detection) that this file itself does not implement beyond one exit-code check.
SUMMARY: Only an ops cron wrapper is delivered; the required Go checks, drills, reconcile/region guard, and tests are absent from the diff, so the acceptance criteria are not demonstrably met.
Even as shipped, the cron file is broken: missing user field, missing env assignments, and a BOM make the schedules unreliable.
Top risks: silently non-executing drills giving false DR confidence, and unattended destructive scratch-DB operations without guardrails.
